entries.name: API Reconnaissance
entries.description: Find all API endpoints supported by the backend server code, documented or undocumented. Find all parameters for each endpoint supported by the backend server, documented or undocumented. Discover interesting data related to APIs in HTML and JavaScript sent to clients.

entries.name: API Broken Object Level Authorization
entries.description: The objective of this test is to identify whether the API enforces proper **object-level authorization** checks, ensuring that users can only access and manipulate objects they are authorized to interact with.

entries.name: Excessive Data Exposure
entries.description: Identify API responses that contain more data than what the client application displays or requires. Detect sensitive fields returned in API responses such as password hashes, authentication tokens, internal object IDs, PII, or infrastructure details. Determine whether the API relies on client-side filtering rather than server-side field selection to control data exposure.

entries.name: API Broken Function Level Authorization
entries.description: The goal of this test is to determine if the API enforces **role or privilege-based access control** to restrict users from accessing or executing functions they are not authorized to use. This ensures that function-level security boundaries are properly enforced.

entries.name: Testing API Authentication Mechanisms
entries.description: Assess whether API keys are scoped, rotated, and transmitted securely. Determine whether bearer tokens are revocable after logout or credential change. Verify that OAuth 2.0 token scope is enforced at the authorization server and the resource server. Evaluate whether APIs that accept session cookies enforce CSRF defenses. Test whether authentication is enforced for every HTTP method on an endpoin…

entries.name: API Rate Limiting and Resource Consumption
entries.description: Verify that per-client and per-endpoint rate limits are enforced. Identify bypass techniques for existing rate limits. Confirm that pagination, batch operations, and query complexity are bounded. Verify that upload size, response size, and timeout controls exist.

entries.name: API Mass Assignment
entries.description: Identify API endpoints that accept structured input (JSON, XML, form-encoded) for object creation or modification. Determine which object properties can be set through client-supplied data by comparing API responses across methods. Confirm whether privileged or internal-only properties are accepted through REST-specific vectors (PUT vs PATCH, nested JSON, content-type switching). Test GraphQL mut…

entries.name: Inbound Webhooks
entries.description: Determine whether inbound webhook endpoints authenticate the sender. Verify tenant, project, and object binding so a valid event for one customer cannot affect another. Verify replay and duplicate-delivery handling. Verify that revoked integrations stop accepting events and remain manageable only by authorized principals.

entries.name: gRPC
entries.description: Identify gRPC and gRPC-Web endpoints and recover the service definitions. Determine whether reflection and built-in services expose information that should not be public. Assess whether authentication and authorization are enforced for every method, call type, and entry point. Assess how the service handles unexpected message content, sizes, and errors.

entries.name: GraphQL
entries.description: Assess that a secure and production-ready configuration is deployed. Validate all input fields against generic attacks. Ensure that proper access controls are applied.

entries.name: Default Credentials
entries.description: Determine whether the application has any user accounts with default passwords. Review whether new user accounts are created with weak or predictable passwords.

entries.name: Weak Lock Out Mechanism
entries.description: Evaluate the account lockout mechanism's ability to mitigate brute force password guessing. Evaluate the unlock mechanism's resistance to unauthorized account unlocking.

entries.name: Bypassing Authentication Schema
entries.description: Ensure that authentication is applied across all services that require it.

entries.name: Vulnerable Remember Password
entries.description: Validate that the generated session is managed securely and do not put the user's credentials in danger.

entries.name: Browser Cache Weaknesses
entries.description: Review if the application stores sensitive information on the client-side. Review if access can occur without authorization.

entries.name: Weak Authentication Methods
entries.description: Determine the resistance of the application against brute force password guessing using available password dictionaries by evaluating the length, complexity, reuse, and aging requirements of passwords.

entries.name: Weak Security Question Answer
entries.description: Determine the complexity and how straight-forward the questions are. Assess possible user answers and brute force capabilities.

entries.name: Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities
entries.description: Determine whether the password change and reset functionality allows accounts to be compromised.

entries.name: Weaker Authentication in Alternative Channel
entries.description: Identify alternative authentication channels. Assess the security measures used and if any bypasses exists on the alternative channels.

entries.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
entries.description: Identify the type of MFA used by the application. Determine whether the MFA implementation is robust and secure. Attempt to bypass the MFA.

entries.name: SAML Authentication
entries.description: Identify the SAML flow in use and the endpoints involved. Determine whether the SP validates the signature, and that the signature covers the data the SP uses. Determine whether the SP enforces the conditions in the assertion (audience, validity period, recipient, and request binding). Assess whether assertions can be replayed or accepted from an untrusted source.

entries.name: Passkeys and WebAuthn
entries.description: Determine whether the RP verifies the challenge, origin and RP ID on registration and authentication. Assess whether recovery and fallback paths weaken the protection that passkeys provide. Determine whether adding, listing and removing credentials is protected. Assess how the RP handles user identification and the data it stores for credentials.

entries.name: OpenID Connect Relying Party
entries.description: Confirm the RP validates issuer discovery and authentication claims before creating a session. Confirm account identity is bound to `(iss, sub)`, not to email alone. Confirm account-linking and recovery flows cannot attach an attacker-controlled identity to another user's account. Confirm mix-up defenses when the RP can use more than one OP. Confirm the RP enforces requested authentication streng…

entries.name: Directory Traversal and File Include
entries.description: Identify injection points that pertain to path traversal. Assess bypassing techniques and identify the extent of path traversal.

entries.name: Bypassing Authorization Schema
entries.description: Assess if unauthenticated, horizontal, or vertical access is possible.

entries.name: Privilege Escalation
entries.description: Identify injection points related to privilege manipulation. Fuzz or otherwise attempt to bypass security measures.

entries.name: Insecure Direct Object References
entries.description: Identify points where object references may occur. Assess the access control measures and if they're vulnerable to IDOR.

entries.name: OAuth Weaknesses
entries.description: Determine if OAuth2 implementation is vulnerable or using a deprecated or custom implementation.

entries.name: Business Logic Data Validation
entries.description: Identify data injection points. Validate that all checks are occurring on the backend and can't be bypassed. Attempt to break the format of the expected data and analyze how the application is handling it. Determine whether parameters that the frontend restricts (type, range, set of allowed values, or relationship to other fields) are restricted again on the server.

entries.name: Ability to Forge Requests
entries.description: Review the project documentation looking for guessable, predictable, or hidden functionality of fields. Insert logically valid data in order to bypass normal business logic workflow.

entries.name: Integrity Checks
entries.description: Review the project documentation for components of the system that move, store, or handle data. Determine what type of data is logically acceptable by the component and what types the system should guard against. Determine who should be allowed to modify or read that data in each component. Attempt to insert, update, or delete data values used by each component that should not be allowed per the…

entries.name: Process Timing
entries.description: Review the project documentation for system functionality that may be impacted by time. Develop and execute misuse cases.

entries.name: Number of Times a Function Can Be Used Limits
entries.description: Identify functions that must set limits to the times they can be called. Assess if there is a logical limit set on the functions and if it is properly validated.

entries.name: Circumvention of Work Flows
entries.description: Review the project documentation for methods to skip or go through steps in the application process in a different order from the intended business logic flow. Develop a misuse case and try to circumvent every logic flow identified.

entries.name: Defenses Against Application Misuse
entries.description: Generate notes from all tests conducted against the system. Review which tests had a different functionality based on aggressive input. Understand the defenses in place and verify if they are enough to protect the system against bypassing techniques.

entries.name: Upload of Unexpected File Types
entries.description: Verify that temporary file references remain bound to the uploading user, original field, and validated file type. Determine whether expired or missing upload metadata causes the application to reject the reference or safely revalidate the underlying file. Check whether references can be reused in fields with different validation requirements or by users who do not own the files. Verify that file…

entries.name: Upload of Malicious Files
entries.description: Identify the file upload functionality. Review the project documentation to identify what file types are considered acceptable, and what types would be considered dangerous or malicious. If documentation is not available then consider what would be appropriate based on the purpose of the application. Determine how the uploaded files are processed. Obtain or create a set of malicious files for tes…

entries.name: Payment Functionality
entries.description: Determine whether the business logic for the e-commerce functionality is robust. Understand how the payment functionality works. Determine whether the payment functionality is secure. Determine whether concurrent requests can bypass limits, reuse single-use values or reach states the workflow should not allow.

entries.name: Denial of Inventory
entries.description: Identify which actions remove business resources from availability. Verify eligibility and aggregate allocation limits across reservation states and booking paths. Demonstrate the effect on another eligible customer and verify recovery.

entries.name: DOM-Based Cross Site Scripting
entries.description: Identify DOM sinks. Build payloads that pertain to every sink type.

entries.name: JavaScript Execution
entries.description: Identify sinks and possible JavaScript injection points.

entries.name: HTML Injection
entries.description: Identify HTML injection points and assess the severity of the injected content. Assess what injected markup can do when script execution is blocked, for example by a Content Security Policy. Determine whether same-origin HTML Injection can undermine CSRF defenses that rely exclusively on HTTP Origin validation. Assess whether XSS can initiate authenticated state-changing requests without addition…

entries.name: Client-side URL Redirect
entries.description: Identify injection points that handle URLs or paths. Assess the locations that the system could redirect to.

entries.name: CSS Injection
entries.description: Identify CSS injection points. Assess the impact of the injection.

entries.name: Client-side Resource Manipulation
entries.description: Identify sinks with weak input validation. Assess the impact of the resource manipulation.

entries.name: Cross Origin Resource Sharing
entries.description: Identify endpoints that implement CORS. Ensure that the CORS configuration is secure or harmless.

entries.name: Clickjacking
entries.description: Assess application vulnerability to clickjacking attacks.

entries.name: WebSockets
entries.description: Identify the usage of WebSockets. Assess its implementation by using the same tests on normal HTTP channels. Verify that authentication and authorization are enforced for the handshake and for every subsequent frame, subscription, and pushed event. Verify that Origin allowlisting uses exact scheme, host, and port comparison.

entries.name: Web Messaging
entries.description: Assess the security of the message's origin. Validate that it's using safe methods and validating its input.

entries.name: Browser Storage
entries.description: Determine whether the site is storing sensitive data in client-side storage. The code handling of the storage objects should be examined for possibilities of injection attacks, such as utilizing unvalidated input or vulnerable libraries.

entries.name: Cross Site Script Inclusion
entries.description: Locate sensitive data across the system. Assess the leakage of sensitive data through various techniques.

entries.name: Reverse Tabnabbing
entries.description: Identify links and `window.open()` calls that open a new tab or window without `noopener`. Assess whether a page opened from the application can change the location of the original page through `window.opener`.

entries.name: Client-side Template Injection
entries.description: Identify the client-side framework and its version used by the application. Detect injection points where user input is reflected into the DOM and processed by the template engine. Assess if the injection allows for arbitrary JavaScript execution (XSS) via the template syntax.

entries.name: DOM Clobbering
entries.description: Identify injection points where user-supplied HTML keeps its `id` or `name` attributes. Identify scripts that read global variables, `document` properties, or form properties that may be undefined, and pass them to sensitive operations. Assess whether clobbering those references changes the behavior of the application.

entries.name: Cross-Site Leaks
entries.description: Identify responses that change with the authenticated user's state or data. Determine whether a cross-site page can observe those differences through browser side channels. Assess whether the application uses the browser defenses that stop cross-site requests or remove the side channels.

entries.name: Client-side Path Traversal
entries.description: Identify inputs that reach the path of a client-side request. Determine which unintended endpoints, methods, and actions those inputs can reach. Assess the impact, including bypass of anti-CSRF defenses and escalation to Cross Site Scripting.

entries.name: Service Workers
entries.description: Identify the service workers an application registers and the scope each one controls. Determine whether an attacker can influence which script is registered, its scope, or the scripts it loads. Assess whether the worker's cache and fetch handling can expose or substitute sensitive responses. Determine whether a worker keeps running after logout or after a vulnerability is fixed.

entries.name: DNS Rebinding
entries.description: Identify services in scope that are reachable only from the local machine or an internal network and are used from a browser. Determine whether those services accept requests with an unexpected `Host` header and without authentication. Determine whether server-side URL fetching can be redirected to internal addresses by changing DNS answers between validation and use.

entries.name: Server-Sent Events
entries.description: Identify the use of Server-Sent Events and how each stream is authenticated. Determine whether a stream can be read from another origin or by another user. Verify that authorization is enforced when the stream is opened, for every event it sends, and after the user's access changes. Assess whether user-controlled data can inject fields or events into the stream, or script into the page that consu…

entries.name: Network Infrastructure Configuration
entries.description: Review the applications' configurations set across the network and validate that they are not vulnerable. Validate that used frameworks and systems are secure and not susceptible to known vulnerabilities due to unmaintained software or default settings and credentials. Where the infrastructure is cloud-hosted or containerized, review network isolation controls (security groups/NSGs, VPC/subnet la…

entries.name: Application Platform Configuration
entries.description: Ensure that default, sample, and known files have been removed from the deployed platform, container image, or serverless package. Validate that no debugging code, debug endpoints, debug modes, or unused modules/dependencies are left enabled in production environments. Review the logging mechanisms set in place for the application, including what sensitive data may be captured and who/what can ac…

entries.name: Review Old Backup and Unreferenced Files for Sensitive Information
entries.description: Find and analyze old, backup, and unreferenced files - including files exposed only through their extension, and objects left in cloud storage - that might contain sensitive information. Validate that no system or framework bypasses exist for any rules put in place to prevent these files from being served.

entries.name: Enumerate Infrastructure and Application Admin Interfaces
entries.description: Identify hidden administrator interfaces and functionality, including cloud, container-orchestration, API-management, and CI/CD management consoles. Check any discovered interface for default, weak, or reused credentials, and for exposure to networks/users beyond those intended.

entries.name: HTTP Methods
entries.description: Enumerate supported HTTP methods. Test for access control bypass. Test HTTP method overriding techniques.

entries.name: HTTP Strict Transport Security
entries.description: Review the HSTS header, its directives, and their values for consistency with current best practice. Confirm the site is protected against the first-request trust gap, either via preload or an otherwise hardened HTTP-to-HTTPS path. Confirm HSTS is applied consistently across the domain and relevant subdomains, and does not mask mixed-content issues.

entries.name: File Permissions
entries.description: Review and identify any rogue file permissions on the host filesystem, in container images/filesystems, and on cloud storage objects. Assess whether Kubernetes volume mounts and `securityContext` settings enforce least-privilege access to files and secrets. Identify secrets stored with overly broad permissions, wherever they are held (filesystem, container image, orchestration secret store, cloud…

entries.name: Subdomain Takeover
entries.description: Enumerate all possible domains (previous and current), including wildcard-covered names. Identify any forgotten or misconfigured domains, and any dangling-service signature not covered by a known response fingerprint. Identify links and resources that point to external domains, buckets, or accounts that no longer exist and could be claimed. Where a takeover is confirmed feasible, assess whether t…

entries.name: Cloud Storage
entries.description: Assess that the access control configuration for the storage services (bucket/container-level public access, and object/principal-level ACLs or IAM policies) is properly in place. Assess whether signed/presigned URLs are scoped, time-limited, and handled appropriately. Assess whether object versioning and lifecycle configuration could expose old or supposedly-removed sensitive data.

entries.name: Content Security Policy
entries.description: Review the Content-Security-Policy header or meta element to identify misconfigurations.

entries.name: Path Confusion
entries.description: Make sure application paths are configured and normalized consistently across all components (application, proxy, cache, CDN, WAF) that make decisions based on the path. Identify cases where trailing slashes, case sensitivity, or encoding differences cause a security control (auth/access rules, routing, cache keying) to be bypassed or behave inconsistently.

entries.name: Additional Browser Security Controls
entries.description: Identify improperly configured security headers. Assess the impact of misconfigured security headers. Validate the correct implementation of required security headers. Identify third-party scripts and style sheets and determine whether they are pinned with Subresource Integrity.

entries.name: Feature Flag Security Bypass
entries.description: Identify feature flags and kill-switches that control security-relevant functionality. Determine whether feature flag states can be manipulated by an unauthorized client, and verify that backend security controls remain enforced independently of client-side flag state. Verify that security controls remain consistently enforced across flag transitions, rollbacks, staged deployments, and services o…

entries.name: Web Cache Poisoning
entries.description: Identify which responses are cacheable and which request inputs form the cache key. Find unkeyed headers, cookies, query parameters, or method-override inputs that change the origin response. Confirm that a clean request without the unkeyed input receives the poisoned or incorrect cached response. Verify that authenticated or personalized responses are not stored under keys reachable by other use…

entries.name: Weak Transport Layer Security
entries.description: Validate the service configuration. Review the digital certificate's cryptographic strength and validity. Ensure that the TLS security is not bypassable and is properly implemented across the application.

entries.name: Padding Oracle
entries.description: Identify encrypted messages that rely on padding. Attempt to break the padding of the encrypted messages and analyze the returned error messages for further analysis.

entries.name: Sensitive Information Sent via Unencrypted Channels
entries.description: Identify sensitive information transmitted through the various channels. Assess the privacy and security of the channels used.

entries.name: Weak Cryptographic Primitives
entries.description: Provide a guideline for the identification weak encryption or hashing uses and implementations. Identify weak digital signature algorithms and missing or incorrect signature verification.

entries.name: Improper Error Handling
entries.description: Identify existing error output. Analyze the different output returned. Determine whether errors expose sensitive information or cause the application to fail open.

entries.name: Role Definitions
entries.description: Identify and document roles used by the application. Attempt to switch, change, or access another role. Review the granularity of the roles and the needs behind the permissions given.

entries.name: User Registration Process
entries.description: Verify that the identity requirements for user registration are aligned with business and security requirements. Validate the registration process.

entries.name: Account Provisioning Process
entries.description: Verify which accounts may provision other accounts and of what type.

entries.name: Account Enumeration and Guessable User Account
entries.description: Review processes that pertain to user identification (*e.g.* registration, login, etc.). Enumerate users where possible through response analysis. Determine whether look-alike or differently normalized identifiers can impersonate, duplicate or take over an existing account.

entries.name: Email Address Verification
entries.description: Determine what an account can do before its email address is verified. Assess whether verification and email change flows bind the proof of ownership to the right address and account. Determine whether an attacker can pre-create or keep access to an account that will belong to the victim. Identify email address syntax that is read differently by the application and by the mail infrastructure, and…

entries.name: Conduct Search Engine Reconnaissance for Information Leakage
entries.description: Identify what sensitive design and configuration information of the application, system, or organization is exposed directly (on the organization's site) or indirectly (via third-party services).

entries.name: Fingerprint Web Server
entries.description: Determine the version and type of a running web server to enable further discovery of any known vulnerabilities.

entries.name: Review Webserver Metafiles for Information Leakage
entries.description: Identify hidden or obfuscated paths and functionality through the analysis of metadata files. Extract and map other information that could lead to a better understanding of the systems at hand.

entries.name: Attack Surface Identification
entries.description: Enumerate all web applications within scope. Identify DNS names, domains, and virtual hosts associated with the target. Discover additional domains and subdomains using passive and active DNS techniques. Analyze digital certificates and Certificate Transparency logs for additional hostnames.

entries.name: Review Web Page Content for Information Leakage
entries.description: Review web page comments, metadata, and redirect bodies to find any information leakage. Gather JavaScript files and review the JS code to better understand the application and to find any information leakage. Identify if source map files or other frontend debug files exist.

entries.name: Identify Application Entry Points
entries.description: Identify possible entry and injection points through request and response analysis.

entries.name: Map Execution Paths Through Application
entries.description: Map the target application and understand the principal workflows.

entries.name: Fingerprint Web Application Framework
entries.description: Fingerprint the components used by the web applications. Identify the versions of those components and determine whether any are outdated, unsupported, or affected by known vulnerabilities.

entries.name: Map Application Architecture
entries.description: Understand the architecture of the application and the technologies in use.

entries.name: Reflected Cross Site Scripting
entries.description: Identify variables that are reflected in responses. Assess the input they accept and the encoding that gets applied on return (if any).

entries.name: Stored Cross Site Scripting
entries.description: Identify stored input that is reflected on the client-side. Assess the input they accept and the encoding that gets applied on return (if any).

entries.name: HTTP Parameter Pollution
entries.description: Identify the back end and the parsing method used. Assess injection points and try bypassing input filters using HPP.

entries.name: SQL Injection
entries.description: Identify SQL injection points. Assess the severity of the injection and the level of access that can be achieved through it.

entries.name: LDAP Injection
entries.description: Identify LDAP injection points. Assess the severity of the injection.

entries.name: XML Injection
entries.description: Identify XML injection points. Assess the types of exploits that can be attained and their severities.

entries.name: SSI Injection
entries.description: Identify SSI injection points. Assess the severity of the injection.

entries.name: XPath Injection
entries.description: Identify XPATH injection points.

entries.name: IMAP SMTP Injection
entries.description: Identify IMAP/SMTP injection points. Understand the data flow and deployment structure of the system. Assess the injection impacts.

entries.name: Code Injection
entries.description: Identify injection points where you can inject code into the application. Assess the injection severity.

entries.name: Command Injection
entries.description: Identify and assess command injection points. Bypass special characters and OS commands filter.

entries.name: Format String Injection
entries.description: Assess whether injecting format string conversion specifiers into user-controlled fields causes undesired behavior from the application.

entries.name: Incubated Vulnerability
entries.description: Identify injections that are stored and require a recall step to the stored injection. Understand how a recall step could occur. Set listeners or activate the recall step if possible.

entries.name: HTTP Response Splitting
entries.description: Identify user-controlled input that is reflected into HTTP response headers. Assess whether CR (`\r`) and LF (`\n`) characters can be injected into response headers. Determine the potential impact of successful HTTP Response Splitting attacks, such as cache poisoning or client-side exploitation.

entries.name: HTTP Request Smuggling
entries.description: Identify request boundary inconsistencies between frontend and backend components Detect classic CL/TE desynchronization vulnerabilities Evaluate protocol translation logic (HTTP/2 → HTTP/1.1) Assess H2C upgrade handling and downgrade safety Identify endpoints that ignore the request body (CL.0) and whether a browser can be made to desynchronize its own connection Confirm backend request queue po…

entries.name: Host Header Injection
entries.description: Assess if the Host header is being parsed dynamically in the application. Bypass security controls that rely on the header.

entries.name: Server-side Template Injection
entries.description: Detect template injection vulnerability points. Identify the templating engine. Build the exploit.

entries.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
entries.description: Identify SSRF injection points. Test if the injection points are exploitable. Asses the severity of the vulnerability.

entries.name: Mass Assignment
entries.description: Identify requests that modify objects Assess if it is possible to modify fields never intended to be modified from outside

entries.name: CSV Injection
entries.description: Identify CSV/spreadsheet export features that include untrusted input. Verify whether attacker-controlled values are interpreted as formulas when the export is opened in common spreadsheet applications. Check whether separator/quote injection can move a dangerous prefix to the start of a cell. Validate whether mitigations remain effective in Microsoft Excel after saving and re-opening the CSV. As…

entries.name: Prototype Pollution
entries.description: Identify functions and libraries that recursively merge, clone, or assign user-controlled properties. Determine whether user input can reach and modify `Object.prototype`. Identify gadgets that turn prototype pollution into a concrete impact.

entries.name: Insecure Deserialization
entries.description: Identify entry points where the application accepts serialized objects from untrusted urces (for example, HTTP headers, parameters, or cookies). Determine the serialization format used by the application. Assess whether serialized input is validated or restricted prior to deserialization. Evaluate whether manipulation of serialized data leads to unsafe behavior or security pact.

entries.name: Server-side URL Redirect
entries.description: Identify request parameters, path segments and headers that control a redirect or forward. Assess whether the validation of redirect targets can be bypassed to reach an external site. Assess whether a redirect can be used to run script, or chained with OAuth, SSO or SSRF.

entries.name: Unicode Normalization and Case Mapping
entries.description: Identify where the application normalizes or changes the case of input. Determine whether validation, filtering or length checks run before that transformation. Assess whether the transformation can be used to bypass filters for injection, path traversal or length limits.

entries.name: JSON Parser Differentials
entries.description: Identify places where the same JSON document is parsed by more than one component. Determine whether those components disagree on duplicate keys, key matching, invalid characters, non-standard syntax, numbers or trailing data. Assess whether a disagreement lets a request pass a check with one value and be processed with another.

entries.name: Server-side Document Rendering Injection
entries.description: Identify features that render user-controlled content into documents or images on the server. Identify the rendering engine and determine whether it processes HTML, CSS, JavaScript, external resources or style sheets supplied by the user. Assess whether the renderer can be used to read local files, reach internal services or run code.

entries.name: Regular Expression Denial of Service
entries.description: Identify inputs that are validated or processed with regular expressions. Determine whether any of those regular expressions take super-linear time on crafted input. Determine whether users can supply their own regular expressions and whether those are run with any limits.

entries.name: Session Management Schema
entries.description: Gather session tokens, for the same user and for different users where possible. Analyze and ensure that enough randomness exists to stop session forging attacks. Modify cookies that are not signed and contain information that can be manipulated.

entries.name: Cookies Attributes
entries.description: Ensure that the proper security configuration is set for cookies.

entries.name: Session Fixation
entries.description: Analyze the authentication mechanism and its flow. Force cookies and assess the impact.

entries.name: Exposed Session Variables
entries.description: Ensure that proper encryption is implemented. Review the caching configuration. Assess the channel and methods' security.

entries.name: Cross Site Request Forgery
entries.description: Determine whether it is possible to initiate requests on a user's behalf that are not initiated by the user.

entries.name: Logout Functionality
entries.description: Assess the logout UI. Verify that the session is properly terminated server-side after logout.

entries.name: Session Timeout
entries.description: Validate that an idle timeout exists and is enforced server-side. Validate that an absolute timeout limits the total lifetime of a session.

entries.name: Session Puzzling
entries.description: Identify all session variables. Break the logical flow of session generation.

entries.name: Session Hijacking
entries.description: Identify vulnerable session cookies. Hijack vulnerable cookies and assess the risk level.

entries.name: JSON Web Tokens
entries.description: Determine whether the JWTs expose sensitive information. Determine whether the JWTs can be tampered with or modified.

entries.name: Concurrent Sessions
entries.description: Evaluate the application's session management by assessing the handling of multiple active sessions for a single user account.

entries.name: WebAssembly Reconnaissance
entries.description: Find all WebAssembly modules loaded by the target application, including those not named `.wasm`, compressed, lazy-loaded, loaded through `fetch`, and manual instantiation, or embedded in JavaScript. Identify the compiler toolchain and source language (e.g., C/C++, Rust, Go, .NET) from section metadata, imports, exports, and glue code. Detect exposed debugging artifacts: source maps, DWARF inform…

entries.name: WebAssembly Static Analysis
entries.description: Identify the module format and enumerate its sections. Inspect imports, exports, types, functions, tables, memory, globals, element segments, code, and data. Convert the binary into readable representations such as WAT, pseudo-code, disassembly, or JavaScript. Map data-segment offsets and inspect retained debug or compiler metadata in depth. Use a controlled modification of a test copy to check w…

entries.name: WebAssembly Dynamic Analysis
entries.description: Intercept the module loading pipeline (`WebAssembly.instantiate`, `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming`, and `new WebAssembly.Instance`) to capture references to active instances and memory segments. Capture and log bidirectional function calls, arguments, memory pointers, and return values crossing the JS/Wasm boundary without violating runtime proxy invariants. Dereference numeric memory pointers…
